item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 represented PDB 1acc chain A as one domain, d1acca_. Newer SCOPe releases retired that whole-chain definition and split chain A into two domains, d1acca1 and d1acca2. Thus, 1accA should no longer be treated as a single evolutionary unit. The revision reflects the principle that a protein chain can contain independently evolving, recombining, and differently conserved structural modules; the split itself does not prove that the two modules are homologous to each other. Homology searches should therefore use each SCOPe domain boundary as a separate query and interpret matches at the domain level. A family-level match can support relatively close homology, a superfamily match supports more remote common ancestry, and a shared fold alone is insufficient evidence of homology or conserved function. Whole-chain searches can miss partial homologs or create misleading composite alignments. Templates and representatives should likewise be selected per domain, with multidomain architecture, linker geometry, and interdomain orientation assessed separately; neither function nor binding specificity should be transferred from one module—or from a fold-only match—to the entire 1accA chain without independent sequence, structural, and functional evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
